transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Um… I guess what brings me in is that I’ve been having a hard time staying seated when I’m supposed to. It’s not like I’m trying to be rude or anything, but during client interviews, tutoring sessions, even book club, I keep finding reasons to get up or move around. People are starting to notice that I can’t just sit and listen, and… I thought maybe I should ask someone about it.
Can you describe what’s going through your mind when you feel the need to get up or move around during those situations?

It’s usually not some big thought like, “I need to leave,” exactly. It’s more like… I start feeling like I just can’t stay put, and then my mind sort of looks for a reason to stand up—get water, check something, grab a file, anything that makes it seem reasonable.

I know I’m supposed to sit and listen, especially with clients or in tutoring, and I do try. I don’t want to come across as disrespectful. But after a bit, staying in the chair feels really uncomfortable, and getting up feels like a relief. Even in book club, where it’s not high pressure, I’ll catch myself shifting around and then popping up for something. People have noticed, which is embarrassing. Does that make sense?
Do you find yourself needing to get up or move around in settings outside of work or book club, like at home or in other social situations?

Um… yes, I think so, though it’s maybe most obvious in the places I mentioned. Like during client interviews or tutoring, I’m supposed to stay put and listen, and I still find myself getting up. And even in book club, which is more social, I’ll do the same thing.

I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but… it does seem to happen whenever I’m expected to just sit still for a while. People are starting to notice, and that’s part of why I came in.
Looking back, did you have similar difficulties staying seated or feeling restless when you were a child, like in school or during family gatherings?

Yes… I mean, I think so. I don’t want to make it sound like I was a terrible kid or anything, because I did well in school, but my report cards in grade school pretty much always said some version of, “bright, but can’t stay in her seat,” or “needs to wait her turn.”

My mother still jokes that I treated every classroom like a crime scene I had to pace through, which is… funny, but also probably tells you something. I guess I’ve always had that restless thing, even back then.
Besides having trouble staying seated, do you find yourself easily distracted, forgetting things often, or feeling like you're constantly 'on the go' as if driven by a motor?

Yes… the “on the go” part, definitely. I mean, I try to make it productive, so it doesn’t look like I’m just bouncing around for no reason.

On days when I don’t have field work, I’ll still move from unpacking boxes to reorganizing case files to suddenly needing to run errands, almost like I’m chasing a lead even when there isn’t one. It’s hard for me to just be off duty and sit still. I don’t know if that’s exactly what you mean, but that’s how it feels.
